formal.visitors: Yes, as the guest of a Christ’s member who books you in on the intranet system; the Christ’s MCR also runs swaps for its own members.
formal.bookingSummary: Christ’s member books you as a guest; MCR swaps
formal.rulesSummary: Formal Hall six nights a week in term, none on Saturdays; students wear gowns. Student guest cap and booking deadline are not published.
formal.formalNights: Six nights a week in term (no Saturdays), dinner from 19:30; MCR Grad Hall on Tuesdays
formal.booking: Host books in the Christ’s intranet meal-booking system (Raven login); student booking deadline not published
formal.dress: Students wear gowns and usually dress smartly; MCR Grad Hall on Tuesdays has no gown or formal dress requirement
formal.price: No dated tariff. Undated college Hall page: about £11.50 for three courses; MCR page (undated): Grad Hall £8.00 for Christ’s members
formal.note:
The college [Meals page](https://www.christs.cam.ac.uk/student-life/meals) quotes a student calling Formal Hall “a great place to invite friends from other colleges”, so attending as a Christ’s member’s guest is the documented route; no public page gives visitors their own booking access. Members book through the intranet meal-booking system linked from the [college’s High Table & Formal Hall page](https://www.christs.cam.ac.uk/high-table-formal-hall); that system needs a Raven login. The [Hall page](https://www.christs.cam.ac.uk/facilities/hall) says Formal Hall runs six nights a week and costs about £11.50 for three courses plus coffee; the page is undated, so treat the price as indicative only. The [alumni booking form](https://www.christs.cam.ac.uk/form/high-table-and-formal-hall) says food is served from 19:30, Formal Hall is term-time only and there is none on Saturdays. Its 14:00, two-days-ahead deadline, guest price and “guests do not need to wear gowns” line apply **to alumni bookings** and are not stated as student rules. No student guest cap or student booking deadline is published.

The [Meals page](https://www.christs.cam.ac.uk/student-life/meals) says students have to wear gowns and people tend to dress smartly; Christmas and Halloween “super halls” cost slightly more. Ask your host whether a guest from another college needs a gown. The [MCR Halls page](https://www.christsmcr.co.uk/halls), which describes itself as informal student guidance, says Grad Hall runs every Tuesday in term: drinks in the MCR at 19:00, a two-course meal around 19:30, £8.00 for Christ’s members, no formal dress or gown requirement. For swaps, the MCR emails its members to sign up and shares out the usually limited places so that everyone can attend at least one; seating-plan changes for special halls close at 13:00 the day before.

**Practical assessment:** find a Christ’s host, or join your own MCR or JCR’s swap with Christ’s. Six weekly sittings make dates easier to find, but the guest allowance and cut-off must come from your host.

formal.visitors: Yes, as a Churchill member’s guest; the host books on the internal Student Hub.
formal.bookingSummary: Churchill member books you on the Student Hub
formal.rulesSummary: Thu, Fri and Sun at 19:30 in term; guest numbers may be limited by demand; one bottle of wine per two diners; no children at formals.
formal.formalNights: Thu, Fri and Sun in term, 19:30
formal.guests: Guests allowed; numbers may be limited by demand. No fixed cap published
formal.booking: Host books on the internal Student Hub (login required); no ordinary booking deadline published
formal.dress: Gowns not required (and not usual); slightly more formal dress encouraged
formal.price: £15.70 students, £16.75 guests (dining page, as at June 2026)
formal.note:
The [Dining page](https://www.chu.cam.ac.uk/about/campus/dining-at-college/) says Formal Hall runs on Thursdays, Fridays and Sundays from 19:30 and sends current students to the internal Student Hub (a login-only SharePoint site) to book. It gives prices of £15.70 for students and £16.75 for guests (as at June 2026). Gowns are not required and slightly more formal dress is encouraged; wine is not provided, but diners may bring strictly limited amounts.

The [2025/26 undergraduate handbook](https://www.chu.cam.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Undergraduate-Handbook-2025-26.pdf) (pp. 24–26 and 40–41) allows guests but says formal hall guest numbers may be limited because of high demand; questions go to catering@chu.cam.ac.uk. No fixed guest cap or ordinary booking deadline is published. Diners may bring **one bottle of wine between two**, and staff may ask rule-breakers to leave. Children may not attend formal halls. Guests’ food allergies must be notified to Catering at least 48 hours ahead. Latecomers wait until the first course is cleared; members pay their guests’ fines. Invitations go out for major Feasts and larger dinners; that is separate from ordinary Formal Hall. University or college societies making block bookings must name a responsible officer, who attends, to Catering at least 24 hours before. The handbook’s prices (£15.40 members, £16.40 guests) are superseded by the June 2026 figures on the dining page.

**Practical assessment:** ask a Churchill member to host you and check the live guest allocation; the college says demand can limit guest places but publishes no sell-out data.

formal.visitors: Yes, as a Clare member’s guest (one per undergraduate via Upay, or an MCR Friday guest ticket); the MCR also runs exchanges with other colleges.
formal.bookingSummary: Clare member books you as a guest; MCR exchanges
formal.rulesSummary: Undergraduate formal Mon–Thu, one guest each via Upay. MCR Friday formal: normally at least one guest; booking Sunday noon to end of Monday.
formal.formalNights: Undergraduate: Mon–Thu in term, 19:30 (arrive by 19:20). MCR: Fridays in term, drinks 19:00, dinner 19:30
formal.guests: Undergraduates: up to 1 guest. MCR members: normally at least one guest ticket
formal.booking: Undergraduates book on Upay, a week or more ahead advised. MCR members use the MCR events booker (Raven login), open Sunday noon to end of Monday
formal.dress: Undergraduate formal: smart; gowns not required by Clare but usually worn. MCR formal: gowns optional but encouraged
formal.price: Undated UCS page: £13.00 for Clare students, guests 'currently £28.00'
formal.note:
The undergraduate [UCS guidance](https://ucs.clare.cam.ac.uk/current-students/life-in-cambridge/) says Formal Hall is open to undergraduates Monday to Thursday in term. Booking is on Upay and each student may bring one guest. The page gives £13.00 for Clare students and says guest tickets are “currently £28.00”, but gives no year, so confirm the price. It warns that some nights fill up fast and suggests booking a week or more ahead. Arrive by 19:20; the meal starts at 19:30. Dress is smart, and gowns are not required by Clare though most people wear them. Wine must be bought from the Buttery before the formal.

[Clare MCR’s Getting Involved page](https://mcr.clare.cam.ac.uk/about/getting-involved) describes a weekly Friday formal in term, usually in the Great Hall: drinks in the MCR from 19:00, dinner at 19:30, gowns optional but encouraged. About a glass of wine each is on the table and members may bring their own within reason. Each MCR member may book one ticket for themselves and normally at least one guest ticket. Places are limited; booking normally opens at noon on the Sunday before and closes at the end of Monday (00:00 Tuesday) through the MCR events booker, which needs a Raven login. The [MCR College Swaps page](https://mcr.clare.cam.ac.uk/social/college-swaps) says swaps are announced by email and booked through the same system; the [2026/27 committee page](https://mcr.clare.cam.ac.uk/about/committees/2026-2027-committee) lists an Exchange Officer who arranges formal dinners with other colleges (mcr-exchanges@clare.cam.ac.uk).

**Practical assessment:** a Clare host is the documented route; no public page lets visitors book for themselves. One guest per undergraduate and the short Friday booking window are the main limits.

formal.visitors: Yes, as a guest of a Clare Hall member who books and pays via Upay; the Graduate Student Body also arranges swaps.
formal.bookingSummary: Clare Hall member books and pays via Upay
formal.rulesSummary: Wednesdays 19:00 for 19:30; students may bring two guests; booking normally closes 15:00 the Monday before, no refunds after.
formal.formalNights: Wednesdays, 19:00 for 19:30
formal.guests: Students up to 2 guests, Seniors 3; more need Domestic Bursar approval; one extra allowed in the quieter summer months
formal.booking: Host books and pays in Upay; normally closes 15:00 the Monday before (feasts: 23:59 seven days before); no refunds after close
formal.dress: Formal dress required (e.g. tailored jacket and tie, trouser suit, skirt or dress); national dress accepted; no shorts, trainers or vests. Feasts: black tie
formal.price: From October 2026 (2026/27 tariff): student £17.50, student’s first guest £21.00, second and further guests £32.00; optional wine £6.00
formal.note:
The [Dining page](https://www.clarehall.cam.ac.uk/dining/) says Formal Hall is every Wednesday, 19:00 for 19:30, with no high table. A member books and pays for themselves and their guests through Upay; tickets are sold first come, first served and can reappear after cancellations. Students may invite **two guests** and Seniors three; more need the Domestic Bursar’s approval, and in the quieter summer months the Upay allowance rises by one. The hall holds 108. Booking typically closes at **15:00 the Monday before** a Formal Hall (feasts close at 23:59 seven days before); there are no refunds after booking closes. Hosts are responsible for their guests’ behaviour and for telling them the dress code. Under-18s may not attend, and phones and tablets may not be used at dining events.

Formal dress is required, for example a tailored jacket and tie, trouser suit, skirt or dress, and national dress is acceptable; shorts, trainers and sleeveless vests can mean refusal of entry. Feasts are black tie. Dietary details go in the Upay booking; strictly kosher meals are not available for guests (questions to formals@clarehall.cam.ac.uk). The Graduate Student Body’s External Officers arrange formal swaps by email. Its once-a-term black-tie Jazz Formals have limited tickets that the college says “sell out extremely quickly”.

**Prices from October 2026:** £17.50 student, £21.00 for a student’s first guest, £32.00 for each further guest; optional wine £6.00 per person. [2026/27 tariff](https://www.clarehall.cam.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Clare-Hall-Meal-Prices-Oct-26.pdf).

**Practical assessment:** ask a Clare Hall member to host you and book before Monday 15:00; a second guest costs noticeably more than the first.

formal.visitors: Yes, as a Corpus student’s guest (up to three); the host books on Upay and must be present at check-in.
formal.bookingSummary: Corpus student books you via Upay; must check in with you
formal.rulesSummary: Fri and Sun in Full Term, 19:30; up to three guests; host must be at check-in; Upay closes Thursday noon; no guests at special formals.
formal.formalNights: Fri and Sun in Full Term, 19:30 (seated before the Fellows enter)
formal.guests: Up to 3 guests per student; more only with the Dean’s advance permission; no guest tickets at special formals such as Bridgemas
formal.booking: Host buys on Upay; sales open 22:00 the Sunday before and close at midday Thursday or when sold out
formal.dress: Jacket and tie or equivalent; gowns for all members of the University, including guests from other colleges
formal.price: 2026-27 rough guide (JCR Finance page): £14.85 student, £21.50 guest
formal.note:
[JCR Catering](https://www.jcr.corpus.cam.ac.uk/catering) says Formal Hall is on Fridays and Sundays in Full Term. Tickets are sold on Upay until they sell out or until **midday on Thursday**, after which they cannot be changed or cancelled. Students can bring up to three guests; more need the Dean’s permission in advance, given only in exceptional circumstances. The college’s [Formal Hall Code of Conduct (April 2024)](https://www.corpus.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/downloads/formal_hall_code_of_conduct_april_2024.pdf) adds that tickets go on sale at 22:00 on the Sunday before. Special formals such as Bridgemas have no guest tickets, and swapping tickets outside Upay’s amendment options is no longer allowed. Guests are admitted only with their host: the Corpus student must be at check-in. Dinner starts promptly at 19:30, everyone must be seated before the Fellows enter, and latecomers are not admitted after First Grace.

The [College Rules (updated 29 June 2026)](https://www.corpus.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/downloads/college_rules.pdf), §18, require smart clothing at the level of a jacket and tie, plus gowns for **members of the University**, so a guest from another Cambridge college should wear one. Students answer for their guests. Each student may bring one 75 cl bottle of wine, or bottled beer, lager or cider up to two pints, and no other alcohol. The [October 2023 Student Accommodation Handbook](https://www.corpus.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/downloads/corpus_handbook_06_oct.pdf) (pp. 18–19) says Upay enrolment is automatic for Corpus students and postgraduate Formal Halls are arranged with the Catering Manager. Its Wednesday-noon amendment cut-off has been replaced by the Thursday-noon cut-off in the 2024 Code of Conduct and on the JCR page. [JCR Finance](https://www.jcr.corpus.cam.ac.uk/finance) lists rough 2026-7 guides of £14.85 for a Formal Hall ticket and £21.50 for a guest; JCR Catering says “around £14” and “£20”.

**Practical assessment:** a Corpus host can bring up to three guests to an ordinary formal, but special formals have no guest places at all.

formal.visitors: Yes, but only as a named guest of a Darwin member who books in Upay and attends with you.
formal.bookingSummary: Darwin member books via Upay and must attend
formal.rulesSummary: Most Wed and Fri, 19:30; up to three guests (one on busy nights such as Burns Night); the host who booked must attend; changes by 14:00 day before.
formal.formalNights: Most Wednesdays and Fridays; check-in from 19:00, dinner 19:30
formal.guests: Up to 3 guests (1 on especially busy nights such as Burns Night or the Christmas Formal Halls); more with Catering Manager permission; guests must be 16+
formal.booking: Host books in Upay (current Darwin members only) with every guest’s full name; cancel or amend by 14:00 the day before
formal.dress: Lounge suit/jacket and tie or equivalent; gowns encouraged for members and for guests who are members of the University; jeans and trainers refused
formal.note:
The [Formal Hall page](https://www.darwin.cam.ac.uk/dine/formal-hall/) says Upay booking is **available to current Darwin members only**. The member who made the booking must accompany their guests; unaccompanied guests are not allowed to dine, and members may not ask other members to book guests for them. A formal dinner is served on most Wednesdays and Fridays, with check-in from 19:00 and dinner at 19:30, for up to 140 diners. Members can book up to **three guests**, but only one on especially busy evenings such as Burns Night or the Christmas Formal Halls; more need the Catering Manager’s permission. Guests must be 16 or over. Every guest’s full name and any dietary requirements must be entered in Upay; the menu is vegetarian by default, with higher-carbon meals an opt-in extra. Bookings can be cancelled or amended until **14:00 the day before**; after that payment is not normally refunded. No price is published; check Upay.

The dress code is a lounge suit or jacket and tie, or an equivalent; members, and guests who are members of the University, are encouraged to wear gowns. A shirt without jacket and tie, jeans, trainers, beach footwear or hats mean refusal of entry. You cannot bring your own wine; buy it through the café after check-in. Student ticket status is checked before admission, and a booking is complete only once the confirmation email arrives. Phones must be off in Hall.

**Practical assessment:** you need a Darwin member who will book you by name and come with you; on the busiest nights each member can bring only one guest.

formal.visitors: Yes: the college describes Formal Hall as an occasion for its students to bring students from other colleges as guests, booked by the Downing host on Upay.
formal.bookingSummary: Downing student books you as a guest on Upay
formal.rulesSummary: Mon, Wed, Fri, Sun in term; up to four guests per host; book, change or cancel by 11:00 two days before; guests wear gowns.
formal.formalNights: Mon, Wed, Fri, Sun in term, 19:30–21:00 (arrive by 19:15)
formal.guests: Up to 4 guests per Downing student (5 places including the host)
formal.booking: Host books on Upay; bookings, changes and cancellations close 11:00 two days before
formal.dress: Gowns throughout dinner for Downing members and their guests from other colleges; smart clothes and smart shoes, no shorts or trainers
formal.note:
The [Catering page](https://www.dow.cam.ac.uk/current-students/catering) describes Formal Hall as an occasion for junior members to bring in students from other colleges and other visitors as guests. It also says Formal Hall charges are lower for College members than for guests, but gives no figure.

[Formal Hall booking](https://www.dow.cam.ac.uk/current-students/catering/formal-hall-booking): Monday, Wednesday, Friday and Sunday evenings in term only, 19:30–21:00. A Downing student books themselves and up to **four guests** (five in total) through Upay. The cut-off is **11:00 two days before** the dinner, and the same cut-off applies to changes and cancellations. Arrive by 19:15 for the 19:30 seating; latecomers are not admitted and are not refunded. Each person may bring one bottle of wine, with no corkage fee. Groups of up to 20 can ask catering@dow.cam.ac.uk to be seated together by the same deadline, giving the full names of all group members; the host still waits for all guests to arrive before going in. Downing groups larger than 20 contact the Internal Events team about a private Formal Hall, non-Downing students are directed to the Conference Office rather than a private formal, and society or external university groups discuss bookings with Internal Events. No route for a non-member to book independently is published.

[Dress and conduct](https://www.dow.cam.ac.uk/current-students/catering/formal-hall-dress-and-conduct): gowns must be worn throughout dinner by members of the College **and their guests from other colleges**. Dress must be smart: collared shirts with a tie or cravat (collarless shirts allowed as cultural dress), smart shoes, no trainers or shorts; clean jeans are acceptable. No drinking games or drinking fines, no electronic devices once dinner begins, and photographs only after the Fellows leave. Staff may ask disruptive or drunk diners to leave, and hosts are responsible for their guests.

The [MCR Social Membership Scheme](https://www.dow.cam.ac.uk/postgraduate-admissions/downing-college-mcr-social-membership-scheme) is for selected postdocs and visiting postgraduate students who are **not already members of another Cambridge college**; social members may bring only one guest. It is not a route for students of other colleges.

**Practical assessment:** four weekly sittings and four guest places give a Downing host plenty of options; the host must book by 11:00 two days ahead, and guests need a gown. No measured sell-out data.

formal.visitors: Yes, as a guest: an Emmanuel student books non-Emmanuel guests through the online system; guests must be over 18 unless the Bursar or Senior Tutor agrees otherwise.
formal.bookingSummary: Emmanuel student books you online as a guest
formal.rulesSummary: Daily except Wed in term, 19:30. Up to 4 guests (Mon, Fri, Sat, Sun) or 10 (Tue, Thu); book by 19:00 three days ahead, groups 10 days ahead.
formal.formalNights: Every evening except Wednesday during the Normal Period of Residence, 19:30 (arrive before 19:15)
formal.guests: Up to 4 non-Emmanuel guests per student on Mon, Fri, Sat, Sun; up to 10 per student on Tue and Thu (club, society and group nights)
formal.booking: Host books online by 19:00 three days (72 hours) ahead; groups at least 10 days ahead. Online cancellation until 18:45 the day before, then email the Head of Catering by 10:00 on the day
formal.dress: Gowns must be worn by members of the College; the 2026/27 guide does not say whether guests wear gowns
formal.note:
The [Domestic Matters (Undergraduates) 2026/2027 guide](https://apps.emma.cam.ac.uk/college/documents/pdfs/FINAL%20-%20DOMESTIC%20MATTERS%202026-27.pdf), dated August 2026, section 29 'Catering arrangements 2026-2027': Formal Hall is at **19:30 every evening except Wednesday** during the Normal Period of Residence; you and your guests must arrive before 19:15 and late arrivals are refused entry. Each Emmanuel student books online for themselves; one student cannot book for another. Monday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday have a limit of **four non-Emmanuel guests** per person; Tuesday and Thursday are open to clubs, societies and groups, with up to **ten guests per Emmanuel student**. Book by **19:00 three days (72 hours) ahead**; group bookings need at least **ten days**. Guests must be over 18 unless the Bursar or Senior Tutor has agreed an exception. Online cancellation is free until 18:45 the day before; after that, email the Head of Catering by 10:00 on the day, after which the meal is charged. Students who started from 1 October 2025 pay through the Pay-As-You-Go system when booking.

Gowns must be worn by members of the College; the guide does not say whether guests must wear them. No toasting, singing or drinking games; photographs only after the Fellows leave or after coffee. Staff refuse admission to anyone not in a fit state, and diners must stay in their seats. Parents' Formal Halls admit close family only, with no other guests.

Booking uses the member portal, which needs a Raven login. No route for a non-member to book independently is published. An [undated Formal Hall leaflet](https://apps.emma.cam.ac.uk/college/documents/pdfs/FORMALS.pdf) gives different group nights and prices and contradicts itself on which nights take groups; rely on the 2026/27 guide. No current price is published. The guide is the undergraduate edition; postgraduate arrangements were not checked.

**Practical assessment:** six formal nights a week and a four-guest quota (ten on Tuesday and Thursday) make it straightforward with a host, but the 72-hour booking deadline, or ten days for groups, means planning ahead. No measured sell-out data.

formal.visitors: Yes, as a guest of a Fitzwilliam member, who waits in the Screens for the guest and presents their University card; Fitz MCR also runs formal swaps with other MCRs.
formal.bookingSummary: Fitz member books you via College Bills, or MCR swap
formal.rulesSummary: Wednesdays and occasional Fridays, 19:30. Host meets guests and shows University card. Super Halls normally one guest; ordinary cap not stated by college.
formal.formalNights: Wednesdays and occasional Fridays in term, 19:30 (in Hall by 19:25)
formal.guests: Ordinary cap not stated in current college documents; Super Halls normally one guest per member (2026/27 Regulations). The MCR page, last updated October 2023, says up to 5
formal.booking: Members-only College Bills portal (Raven login). Postgraduates are asked to book at least 48 hours ahead (2026/27 welcome pack); the MCR page (2023) says bookings and cancellations close 14:00 two days before
formal.dress: Gowns worn, with jacket, collar and tie, cultural dress or smart evening wear (2026/27 Regulations); older MCR pages say guests need not wear gowns
formal.note:
The college [Food and drink page](https://www.fitz.cam.ac.uk/cafe-bar-and-buttery) says Formal Halls, open to the whole College, are traditionally held on **Wednesdays and occasional Fridays**, and its booking link is labelled 'Book for Formal (Members only)'; it goes to College Bills, which needs a Raven login. Guests from other colleges therefore attend through a Fitzwilliam host.

The [2026/27 College Regulations](https://www.fitz.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2026-10/College%20Regulations%20for%202026-27_FINAL.pdf) (paragraph 62 and Appendix 4) say guests of Fitzwilliam members may attend, and Super Halls are normally limited to one guest per member. Entry is by University card: the host waits in the Screens for their guest and presents their card. Diners must be in Hall by 19:25; those arriving after 19:30 may be refused. Anyone who appears intoxicated is refused entry. One bottle of wine per diner may be brought in, no beer containers, and no alcohol is served from the Bar during dinner. Coining or other incitement to excessive drinking leads to ejection. Diners should generally be over 18, or over 16 with a host over 18. Dress should suit the occasion (jacket, collar and tie, cultural dress or smart evening wear) and gowns are worn; the regulations do not say whether guests are exempt.

The [2026 postgraduate welcome pack](https://www.fitz.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2026-08/2026%20Welcome%20Pack.pdf) asks postgraduates to book at least 48 hours ahead and says places are first come, first served. It no longer gives a maximum number of places.

Older MCR pages differ in places. The [MCR Formal Hall page](https://mcr.fitz.cam.ac.uk/overview/formal-hall/), last updated October 2023, lists Wednesdays and Fridays, up to **five guests**, bookings and cancellations until 14:00 two days before, gowns for College members only (not guests), and formals by arrangement for at least 20 people. An [MCR FAQ from 2018](https://mcr.fitz.cam.ac.uk/faq/formal-hall-work/) also says guests need not wear gowns. On swaps, the [MCR swaps page](https://mcr.fitz.cam.ac.uk/overview/college-swaps/) says you book only yourself, with no guests, and the [MCR FAQ](https://mcr.fitz.cam.ac.uk/faq/whats-the-best-way-to-attend-formals-at-other-colleges/) aims for three swaps a term and warns they sell out fast. Confirm the guest cap and deadline with the host for the current term. No current price is published.

**Practical assessment:** one regular formal night a week plus occasional Fridays, booked only by a member through a Raven-protected portal; ask the host to confirm the current guest cap and whether guests need gowns. No measured sell-out data.

formal.visitors: Yes, as a named guest of a Girton student booked on Upay; the college mentions inviting guests from other colleges.
formal.bookingSummary: Girton student books you through Upay
formal.rulesSummary: Thursdays in term; up to two named guests where guests are permitted; Upay opens Thu 08:00 a week ahead and closes Tue 12:00.
formal.formalNights: Thursdays in term (occasionally changed for special events); drinks from about 18:45, dinner 19:15–19:30
formal.guests: Up to 2 named guests per student, at formals where guests are permitted
formal.booking: Upay; opens Thursday 08:00 one week before and closes Tuesday 12:00 (two days before). Refundable until booking closes; tickets are non-transferable
formal.dress: Gowns worn at Thursday formals; the 2024 Freshers' Guide calls the dress code smart (suits and ties, dresses or traditional wear)
formal.note:
The [incoming postgraduate guide](https://www.girton.cam.ac.uk/postgraduates/incoming-postgraduates/about-university-and-college) says formals are typically held every Thursday in term (occasionally altered for special events), with drinks from around 18:45 and dinner from 19:15–19:30. Upay booking opens on **Thursday at 08:00 one week before** and closes at **12:00 on the Tuesday**. A student may bring **up to two named guests** to formals where guests are permitted. Tickets are non-transferable but refundable while booking is open. Ticket prices for **2026/27** are £16 for students and £24 for guests. Postgraduates are invited to join any Fellows dining on High Table. The Matriculation Dinner and College Feast are by invitation for Girton students. Booking queries go to catering@girton.cam.ac.uk.

[Dining and Socialising](https://www.girton.cam.ac.uk/dining-and-socialising) says gowns are worn at Thursday formals and mentions the opportunity to invite guests from other colleges. No route for a non-member to book independently is published.

The [2024 Freshers' Guide](https://www.girton.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2024-09/Girton%20Freshers%27%20Guide%202024.pdf) adds: bring your CamCard, accompany your guests, smart dress (suits and ties, dresses or traditional wear) plus a gown, and pay corkage in Schlub for wine not bought in college. It warns tickets can sell out fast. These 2024 details should be confirmed with the host.

**Practical assessment:** one weekly sitting and two guest places limit the options; ask the host to book when Upay opens on Thursday morning. No measured sell-out data.

formal.visitors: Yes, as a guest of a Caius student (the college says students often invite friends from other colleges); postgraduates can also come on a Caius MCR formal swap, usually at a Superhall.
formal.bookingSummary: Caius student books you as a guest; MCR swaps
formal.rulesSummary: Formal (Second) Hall 19:20, usually six nights a week in term; gowns for all University members. Guest cap and deadline only on a 2022 JCR page.
formal.formalNights: Usually six nights a week in term (MCR: every night except Saturday), Second/Formal Hall at 19:20
formal.guests: Not stated on current college pages; the GCSU (JCR) food page, last updated December 2022, says up to 2 guests per meal
formal.booking: Host books online (college 'Booking meals online' link goes to Upay; the JCR calls it the Meal Booking System). JCR page (2022): opens about 4 days before, closes 10:00 on the day
formal.dress: Members of the University, including students from other colleges, must wear gowns at Formal Hall (including Guest Nights) in Full Term; no other dress code for ordinary Formal Hall
formal.note:
The college [Hall page](https://www.cai.cam.ac.uk/living-here/food-and-drink/hall) says there are two evening sittings, usually on six nights a week: Second, or Formal, Hall is at **19:20**, students wear gowns, and there is no other dress code. It does not name the six nights. The [Food and drink page](https://www.cai.cam.ac.uk/living-here/food-and-drink) says students book through an online system and often invite friends from other colleges, for example for birthdays; it also mentions a twice-termly Superhall. The site-wide 'Booking meals online' link goes to Upay, which needs a login. A Caius host is therefore the documented route; no route for a non-member to book independently is published.

The [College Regulations](https://www.cai.cam.ac.uk/discover/strategy-and-policies/statutes-ordinances-regulations-and-handbooks/college-regulations), last updated by the College Council on **20 October 2026**, require **members of the University** to wear gowns when dining at Formal Hall, including Guest Nights, during Full Term. This covers students visiting from other colleges.

The [GCSU (JCR) food page](https://jcr.cai.cam.ac.uk/college-life/food-bar/), last updated December 2022, says booking on the Meal Booking System typically opens four days before and closes at 10:00 on the day for dinner; a student can bring **up to two guests** per meal; up to half a bottle of wine per person may be brought, with corkage unless bought at the College Bar; and diners scan their CamCard on entry. Its guest and corkage prices date from 2022, so no current price is given here; confirm the guest cap with the host.

The [MCR dining page](https://mcr.cai.cam.ac.uk/index.php/prospective/dining/) says Formal Hall runs every night in term except Saturday, apart from special dinners. MCR Superhalls are twice per Full Term, four courses, MCR-only, black tie and no gowns. The MCR Dining Officers (mcr-dining@cai.cam.ac.uk) organise formal swaps, with visiting postgraduates typically dining at a Superhall; ask your own MCR. For Superhall dress, follow the organiser's instructions.

**Practical assessment:** frequent sittings give a Caius host many dates to choose from, but bring a gown and confirm the guest cap and deadline with the host. No measured sell-out data.

formal.visitors: Yes, as a guest: the college says members can buy guest tickets on Upay for friends who do not attend Homerton.

formal.rulesSummary: Tuesdays 19:30 in Full Term; usually 2 guest tickets; tickets out 18:00 eight days ahead, close the Friday before; CamCards checked, no ticket swaps.

Gowns are welcome but not required. No route for a non-member to book independently is published.

The [MCR Formal Hall Dates page](https://homerton-mcr.co.uk/formal-hall-dates), headed 2026/27, says regular formals are every **Tuesday** of Full Term at **19:30**, open to undergraduates and postgraduates. Postgraduate-only formals fall on selected other nights (19:00 drinks, 19:30 dinner); check exact dates on Upay, since the MCR list and the [college's Michaelmas 2026 menu list](https://www.homerton.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2026-11/formal-menus-Michalemas-term-2026-for-website.docx) differ on one of them. Its FAQ says there is usually the option of **two guest tickets**, at **£20 for Homerton students and £24 for guests**. Tickets typically come out **at 18:00 eight days before** and, it says, typically sell out very fast. Regular formals include wine and soft drinks; semi-formals have two courses and no drinks. There is no dress code and no gown requirement. Special formals, including matriculation dinners, are typically by invitation.

The [HUS (JCR) food page](https://www.hus-jcr.co.uk/college-life/food/) says undergraduate booking opens at 18:00 on the Monday of the week before and **closes the preceding Friday**. **Ticket swapping is no longer possible because CamCards are checked** on arrival; refunds go through the Finance team. It also lists Thursday semi-formals at 19:30. Follow this over the MCR's mention of people selling tickets in the MCR chat: get a genuine guest booking. The public pages do not say whether the host must attend with the guest, or set an alcohol limit.

**Practical assessment:** one regular formal a week and usually two guest tickets, released eight days ahead and closing the Friday before; ask the host to book at release. No measured sell-out data.

formal.visitors: Yes, as the personal guest of a Hughes Hall member who books and attends with you; MCR swaps and other larger groups need approval via formal.hall@hughes.cam.ac.uk.
formal.bookingSummary: Hughes member books you as a personal guest in Upay
formal.rulesSummary: Usually Tue and Fri in term; up to three guests, host must attend; book by 10:00 on the Friday (for Tue) or Tuesday (for Fri) before.
formal.formalNights: Usually Tue and Fri in term time; drinks 19:00, dinner 19:30
formal.guests: Up to 3 guests per student (some popular evenings have tighter limits); larger groups need approval
formal.booking: Upay, paid from meal credit; Tuesday formal by 10:00 the preceding Friday, Friday formal by 10:00 the preceding Tuesday
formal.dress: Lounge suit (jacket and tie) or equivalent; no jeans, T-shirts or trainers; gowns optional
formal.price: £17 students, £20 per guest (no year given; page last updated 12 Aug 2026)
formal.note:
Formal Hall is **open to members of Hughes Hall and their personal guests only**; guests can attend only with the member hosting them, and a host who cannot come cannot send guests alone. Formals are usually on **Tuesdays and Fridays in term**: drinks at 19:00 in the Peter Richards Room, dinner in Hall at 19:30. On arrival the Porter checks the reservation and number of guests, and the group must meet before joining drinks. [Formal Halls](https://www.hughes.cam.ac.uk/student-centre/practical/dining/formal-halls/).

Book and prepay in **Upay** from meal credit. Deadlines: Tuesday formal by **10:00 the preceding Friday**; Friday formal by **10:00 the preceding Tuesday**. Each student may bring **up to three guests** (up to four places); some popular evenings have tighter limits. Larger groups, such as MCR swaps organised by the External Social Secretary, recognised Hughes societies or PhD research groups, must be approved via formal.hall@hughes.cam.ac.uk. Bookings are personal and non-transferable and may not be resold; the Conference Office may be able to reassign a ticket if asked by 14:30 the day before. Hosts wishing to bring under-18 guests should check with the College in good time. The page lists **£17 for students and £20 per guest** without stating a year (page last updated 12 August 2026). [Formal Halls](https://www.hughes.cam.ac.uk/student-centre/practical/dining/formal-halls/).

Dress: lounge suit (jacket and tie) or equivalent; no jeans, T-shirts or trainers; gowns optional. Hosts are responsible for their guests' behaviour; phones off or silent. [Formal Halls](https://www.hughes.cam.ac.uk/student-centre/practical/dining/formal-halls/).

**Practical assessment:** a student from another college needs a Hughes Hall member to book and attend with them, a few days ahead of the published deadline; groups and swaps need prior approval.

formal.visitors: Yes, as one of up to three guests of a Jesus member who books via Upay; no public route for booking on your own.
formal.bookingSummary: Jesus member books you as a guest via Upay
formal.rulesSummary: Tue, Wed, Fri and Sun at 19:30 (postgraduates dine separately on Wed); up to three guests; cut-offs and prices are only on JNet (login).
formal.formalNights: Tue, Wed, Fri and Sun at 19:30; postgraduates dine separately on Wednesdays in Upper Hall
formal.guests: Up to 3 guests per member
formal.booking: Upay, with dietary details added to the booking; the college advises booking up to seven days ahead, especially for Sundays and themed dinners; deadlines are not published publicly
formal.dress: Suit and tie or cocktail dress; students and Fellows wear academic gowns
formal.note:
Formal Hall runs **four times a week at 19:30: Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday and Sunday**; postgraduates dine separately on Wednesdays in Upper Hall. A member can bring **up to three guests**, who must know and follow the dress code and the code of conduct. Bookings, including dietary details, are made on **Upay**. The college suggests booking **up to seven days ahead**, especially for Sundays and themed dinners; this is advice, not a stated deadline. Key dates and prices are on JNet, the College intranet, which needs a login. No public route for booking without a Jesus host is described. [Official Formal Hall page](https://www.jesus.cam.ac.uk/college/life-jesus/food-and-drink/formal-hall).

The college recommends arriving before 19:15 as there is often a queue; everyone must be seated by 19:30, when the Master says grace. Dress is suit and tie or cocktail dress; students and Fellows wear gowns. Iced water is provided; diners may bring soft drinks and **up to one 750ml bottle of wine per person**, and the College bar sells wine. Public guidance does not set out host check-in or ID rules. Enquiries: manciple@jesus.cam.ac.uk. [Official Formal Hall page](https://www.jesus.cam.ac.uk/college/life-jesus/food-and-drink/formal-hall).

**Practical assessment:** you need a Jesus member to book you as one of their three guests on Upay; with four formals a week, booking about a week ahead is the college's own advice.

formal.visitors: No public rule; the only documented route is KiFoMaSy, which needs a login, so ask a King's student or KCSU/KCGU whether guest tickets are offered for a given formal.
formal.bookingSummary: King's member books via KiFoMaSy (KCSU/KCGU formals)
formal.rulesSummary: Formals are run by KCSU and KCGU and sold through KiFoMaSy, which needs a login; guest numbers, prices, dates and dress are not published.
formal.booking: KiFoMaSy (store.kcsu.org.uk, login required); details of student formals are sent by email
formal.note:

[Student Hub](https://www.kings.cam.ac.uk/student-hub), [KCSU](https://www.kcsu.org.uk/). KiFoMaSy itself requires a login, so no guest quota, price, dates, dress code or outside-student booking rule is publicly visible. Ask a King's host or KCSU/KCGU about guest tickets for the formal you want.

The **2025 Annual Report** says the unions renegotiated the memorandum of understanding for student-run formals, with guaranteed tickets for each union and free tickets for the students running the event. The College agreed **in principle to two student-run formals a week, funding permitting**; funding for a permanent expansion was not secured that year. An extra graduate formal was approved in Easter Term. [Annual Report 2025](https://kingscollege.shorthandstories.com/kings-college-cambridge-annual-report-2025/index.html).

**Practical assessment:** the route runs through a King's student and a login-only ticketing system; no public rule tells an outside student whether or how they can get a ticket.

formal.visitors: Yes: the college expects visitors from other Cambridge colleges (they must wear gowns), normally booked as a Lucy member's guest; a visitor log-in exists but its password comes from the Finance Office.
formal.bookingSummary: Lucy member books you as a guest in the college portal
formal.rulesSummary: Thu and Fri in term; up to five guests online; book, change or cancel by 12:00 two days before; gowns required, including for visiting students.
formal.formalNights: Thu and Fri during term; drinks 19:00 in Warburton Hall, dinner 19:30
formal.guests: Up to 5 guests booked online by a member; larger groups need the Steward's approval; no children under 16
formal.booking: College portal (services.lucy.cam.ac.uk), paid from EPOS meals funds; closes 12:00 Tue for Thu and 12:00 Wed for Fri; no refund after the deadline
formal.dress: Smart but not black tie; gowns for all University members, including visitors from other colleges; black tie encouraged at Superformals

Formal Hall is on **Thursday and Friday evenings in term**: drinks at 19:00 in Warburton Hall, dinner at 19:30. Dress is smart but not black tie; **academic gowns must be worn by all members of the University, including visitors from other Cambridge colleges**. At Superformals black tie is encouraged but optional; gowns remain mandatory. Guests should stay seated between the two graces and keep phones away. [Formal Hall](https://www.lucy.cam.ac.uk/formalhall), [FAQs](https://www.lucy.cam.ac.uk/formal-hall-faqs).

Members may book **up to five guests online**; larger groups need the Steward's approval via formalhall@lucy.cam.ac.uk. The deadline is **12:00 on Tuesday for Thursday and 12:00 on Wednesday for Friday**; changes and cancellations are possible until then, with no refund afterwards. When a formal is full there is a queue, filled one place at a time, so part of a group may get in; funds must stay on the EPOS account. For group or reserved bookings, names, diets and seating must be confirmed by the Friday of the week before. Children under 16 are not admitted. [Formal Hall](https://www.lucy.cam.ac.uk/formalhall), [FAQs](https://www.lucy.cam.ac.uk/formal-hall-faqs).

Booking is through the **[college portal](https://services.lucy.cam.ac.uk/)**, paid from EPOS meals funds topped up first; the portal says 2026/27 formals are open for booking. Raven users log in with Raven; visitors without Raven use the visitor log-in, for which the Finance Office (financeoffice@lucy.cam.ac.uk) issues a password. The booking guide (dated May 2023) says a member must book themselves before adding guests, up to five. [Portal](https://services.lucy.cam.ac.uk/), [Visitor log-in](https://services.lucy.cam.ac.uk/meal-epos/), [Booking guide](https://www.lucy.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/inline-files/Formal%20hall%20and%20meals%20top%20up%20guide_0.pdf).

A glass of sherry or an alcohol-free option is included on arrival; wine is extra. BYO wine pays corkage, and consumption is limited to **one bottle shared between three people**. The FAQ gives **2025/26** prices: £18.07 for Lucy students, £21.68 for guests of students, £32.39 for others; Superformals £30.94, £34.56 and £45.27. Check the portal for current prices. [FAQs](https://www.lucy.cam.ac.uk/formal-hall-faqs).

**Practical assessment:** a Lucy member can book you as one of five guests up to two days ahead; visiting students must bring a gown. Without a host, ask formalhall@lucy.cam.ac.uk, since the visitor log-in alone does not show that outside students may book.

formal.visitors: Yes, as the guest of a Magdalene member who books via Upay and comes into Hall with you; Friday BA dinners are open to MCR students and their guests.

formal.rulesSummary: UG halls Tue/Thu/Sun, MCR BA dinners Fri, 19:30. Hosts must come in with guests. Code: up to 10 guests Mon–Wed, 2 Thu–Sun; MCR page says 2.
formal.formalNights: Undergraduate formals Tue, Thu, Sun at 19:30 (JCR page); MCR BA dinners on Fridays at 19:30 in term
formal.guests: College Code of Practice: up to 10 guests Mon–Wed, up to 2 Thu–Sun (parents not counted); MCR page: 2 guests per student; no under-13s
formal.booking: Upay; the JCR page says by 12:00 the day before, the 2024/25 Student Guide says 18:00 the day before

formal.price: JCR page (undated): £12.00 Magdalene students, £19.70 guests; 2025/26 Accommodation Handbook: £11.65 and £19.35 (incl. VAT)

The JCR lists undergraduate formals on **Tuesday, Thursday and Sunday at 19:30**, booked in **Upay by 12:00 the day before**. Its undated prices are **£12.00 for Magdalene students and £19.70 for guests**. Dress is smart and members wear gowns. Buttery wine is sold; BYO wine carries **£3.50 corkage**. [JCR catering](https://www.jcr.magd.cam.ac.uk/catering). The 2024/25 Student Guide instead lists Formal Hall on Tuesday, Thursday, Friday and Sunday, with a booking and cancellation deadline of **18:00 the day before**; the 2025/26 Accommodation Handbook lists £11.65 and £19.35 (guest, incl. VAT). [Student Guide 2024/25](https://www.magd.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2025-04/student_guide_2024-25.pdf), [Accommodation Handbook 2025/26](https://www.magd.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2025-08/Accommodation_Handbook_2025-26.pdf).

The College's **Code of Practice for Dinner in Hall** allows **up to ten guests Monday to Wednesday and up to two Thursday to Sunday** (parents not counted) and says **students must come in with their guests** and remain liable for them. Members must wear gowns, and guests who are University members are encouraged to. Guests under 13 are not admitted. Diners may bring at most **one bottle of wine per head**. Latecomers are not admitted after the doors shut at 19:30, and phones must be off. Apart from the Friday graduate table, Hall is not available for group bookings. [Code of Practice](https://www.magd.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2025-06/code_of_practice_for_dinner_in_college_hall.pdf).

The MCR says **every student can book two guests** and that Friday **BA dinners** are for MCR students, with drinks before and after; its prices (£16.00 BA, £11.00 other nights) are dated 2024. Current listings show BA dinners on 13, 20 and 27 November 2026 at 19:30, open to students and their guests, formal dress with gowns, booked via Upay, with free pre-drinks in Benson Hall from 18:45 and port in the MCR afterwards. [MCR food](https://www.mcr.magd.cam.ac.uk/food-drink), [BA dinner, 13 Nov 2026](https://www.mcr.magd.cam.ac.uk/events/ba-formal-dinner-in-hall-hdw54-8wc4j-dfy83-w9sg8-3xrar-wcx6d), [MCR events](https://www.mcr.magd.cam.ac.uk/events).

**Practical assessment:** a Magdalene member must book you on Upay and come into Hall with you; confirm the guest limit and deadline with them, as the official pages differ.

formal.rulesSummary: College says students may invite friends from other colleges; the 2024/25 packs cap guests at 3 (UG) or 2 (PG), and 1 at Super Hall.

The current **college facilities page** says the Dome hosts weekly themed formals and that students **can invite as many friends as they want from other colleges**. This describes a hosted guest route, not booking by outsiders. [College facilities](https://www.murrayedwards.cam.ac.uk/college-life/college-facilities).

The most recent detailed rules are in the **2024/25 Freshers' Packs**, still the packs linked from the college's Freshers page. Formal Hall is on **Tuesdays and the first Friday of each month in full term**. Undergraduates may book **up to three guests**, postgraduates **up to two**, and everyone **one** at Super Halls. Block bookings: undergraduates up to 12 places plus the booker, by form at least 10 days ahead; postgraduates up to 10 places including the booker. Super Halls have no group bookings. Bookings open at the start of term and close at **12:00 on Sunday for Tuesday** and **14:00 on Wednesday for Friday**. [UG pack 2024/25](https://www.murrayedwards.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2024-08/UG%20Freshers%27%20Pack%202024.pdf), [PG pack 2024/25](https://www.murrayedwards.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2024-08/PG%20Freshers%27%20Pack%202024.pdf), [Freshers page](https://www.murrayedwards.cam.ac.uk/node/27).

The packs also say: always wear a gown; dress shoes only, no trainers; tickets are collected from 18:45 by the Fellows' Dining Room with College ID; postgraduates go up to the Dome at 19:10; college rules allow half a bottle of wine per person; latecomers may be refused. Their prices are for 2023-24 and are not repeated here. Questions go to catering@murrayedwards.cam.ac.uk. [PG pack 2024/25](https://www.murrayedwards.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2024-08/PG%20Freshers%27%20Pack%202024.pdf). These dining sources do not restrict guests by gender.

**Practical assessment:** the college explicitly welcomes friends from other colleges, but a Murray Edwards student must book you; confirm the current guest limit, since the facilities page and the 2024/25 packs differ.

formal.visitors: Yes, as the guest of a Newnham member who books and attends with you, or through a JCR/MCR swap agreed with Catering before term; guests cannot attend Subject Formal Halls.
formal.bookingSummary: Newnham host books and attends; or JCR/MCR swap
formal.rulesSummary: Host must attend. UG halls: 2 guests (3 at the termly Friday hall); PG halls: 3. Booking opens Monday 17:00 the week before.
formal.formalNights: Regular halls about 1-2 a week (dates on the members' portal); graduate halls every other Tuesday; dinner 19:30
formal.guests: Undergraduate-bookable halls: up to 2 guests (3 at the once-a-term Friday hall); postgraduate halls: up to 3; host must attend
formal.booking: Members' meal portal (login); opens Monday 17:00 the week before, closes Wednesday 22:00; charged to the College bill
formal.dress: Gowns to be worn; guest gown rule not stated
formal.price: Member £19.90, non-member £24.90 (undated College food-and-drink page, as shown on 7 Nov 2026)
formal.note:
**Formal dinners are private events and a Newnham host must be present.** Under the [ticket policy, updated 5 May 2026](https://newn.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2026-05/policy-re-formal-hall-tickets-speakers.pdf), an undergraduate may buy **three tickets including their own (two guests)**, or four (three guests) at the Friday hall held normally once a term. A postgraduate may buy **four tickets including their own (three guests)** for postgraduate halls, which only postgraduates may book. Bookings open at **17:00 on the Monday one week before**, and tickets are charged to the College bill. Arrive in Hall by **19:15** to check in; gowns are worn; each person may bring half a bottle of wine, with no corkage. Matriculation Feast, Half-Way Hall and Subject Formal Halls are by named invitation and cannot be passed on, sold or swapped. JCR or MCR swaps are allowed when organised through the committee and agreed with the Catering Operations Manager (catman@newn.cam.ac.uk) before the start of term, usually for up to 15-20 (JCR) or 30 (MCR) places.

The College's [food and drink page](https://newn.cam.ac.uk/study-here/life-newnham/societies-and-facilities/food-and-drink) (undated) says bookings close at **22:00 on the Wednesday of the week before**, dinner starts at 19:30, every guest must be accompanied by their host, and lists **£19.90 member / £24.90 non-member**. The [student eating page](https://newn.cam.ac.uk/student-hub/living-college/eating-drinking-and-events) adds that doors close at 19:30, guests cannot enter late or without their host, groups wanting to sit together should arrive by 19:00, drinking games are banned, and guests cannot attend Subject Formal Halls. The [MCR page](https://newnhammcr.soc.srcf.net/formal-hall.html) says regular formals are typically held once or twice a week, graduate formals every other Tuesday, and that students from other subjects may sign up for a subject hall with guests if space allows; this conflicts with the College page, so follow the College rule. Booking is through the members-only [meal portal](https://foodanddrink.newn.cam.ac.uk/).

**Practical assessment:** you need a Newnham member to book you and attend, or a place on a JCR/MCR swap; caps are two or three guests per host and booking closes the week before the hall.

formal.visitors: Yes, as a guest booked by a Pembroke member who is responsible for your conduct; groups of ten or more need advance permission and are limited to Monday nights.
formal.bookingSummary: Pembroke host books in Upay; groups via Catering
formal.rulesSummary: Over 3 guests via Catering; groups of 10+ on Mondays only, need Catering and Registrar approval and 1 Pembroke steward per 9 guests.
formal.formalNights: Usually Sun, Mon, Tue, Thu at 19:30 in term (may vary); graduate BA Dinner on Fridays; be at your table by 19:15
formal.guests: Per-host cap not published; bookings with more than 3 guests go through Catering
formal.booking: Upay; tickets go on sale a week before (GP guide 2026); larger groups via formal@pem.cam.ac.uk, paid in full before booking
