formal.note:
The [Graduate Parlour welcome guide 2026](https://www.pem.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/downloads/grad_welcome_document_2026.docx.pdf) says ordinary formal is at **19:30**, usually on **Sunday, Monday, Tuesday and Thursday** (this may vary year to year), with a graduate-only BA Dinner every Friday. Tickets are bought through Upay and go on sale **a week before**; dress is formal and academic gowns are required. The College's [student prices page](https://www.pem.cam.ac.uk/current-students/finance-information/student-prices) gives **2026-27 prices of £15 student / £27.30 guest**, repeated on the [postgraduate page](https://www.pem.cam.ac.uk/study-here/postgraduate); the GP guide's older 'about £12 / £25.50' should not be used. The [College bill page](https://www.pem.cam.ac.uk/current-students/finance-information/college-bills/understanding-college-bill) says bookings with **more than three guests** go through Catering (formal@pem.cam.ac.uk) and must be paid in full before they are booked. No per-host guest cap or final booking deadline is published.

The [Formal Hall procedure](https://www.pem.cam.ac.uk/college/catering/information-students/formal-hall-procedure) (undated) says diners should be at their table by **19:15**. **Groups of ten or more**, from Pembroke or including guests (Monday nights only), need advance permission from Catering, then from the College Registrar, and must name one Pembroke student as host and steward for every nine guests. Pembroke students must wear gowns; no baseball caps; no more than one bottle of wine per person and no spirits or cans of beer; no photography during dinner, no phone use and no games at table. Hosts are responsible for their guests' conduct on College premises. The [facilities booking page](https://www.pem.cam.ac.uk/current-students/how-book-pembrokes-facilities) links the Formal Hall permission form, and the [stewards guidance for 2026-27](https://www.pem.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/downloads/stewards_and_permissions_26-27.pdf) confirms one steward per nine other attendees, all Pembroke members.

**Practical assessment:** you need a Pembroke member to book you through Upay; groups over three guests go through Catering, and groups of ten or more need two approvals, Monday-night booking and Pembroke stewards.

formal.visitors: Yes, as the guest of a Peterhouse member who books on Upay and attends the whole dinner; guests whose host does not attend are refused without refund.
formal.bookingSummary: Peterhouse host books in Upay and must attend
formal.rulesSummary: 2026/27: max 2 guests per member; host must admit guests and stay for dinner; booking closes 11:00 the day before.
formal.formalNights: 19:30 in Full Term; bookable dates listed on Upay
formal.guests: Up to 2 guest tickets per Junior Member (2026/27 handbooks)
formal.booking: Upay; opens one week ahead, closes 11:00 the previous day; no changes or refunds after it closes
formal.dress: Junior Members must wear gowns at Formal Hall and Super-Hall; guest gown rule not stated
formal.price: 2026/27: £9.75 member; £16.45 per guest including VAT (2026/27 student handbooks)
formal.note:
The **2026/27** [Undergraduate](https://www.pet.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2026-10/UG%20handbook%202026_Final.pdf) and [Postgraduate](https://www.pet.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2026-10/PG%20handbook%202026_Final.pdf) Student Handbooks (linked from the [handbooks page](https://www.pet.cam.ac.uk/student-handbooks-college-regulations-and-procedures)) give the current rules. Formal Hall is at **19:30 in Full Term**, with bookable dates on Upay. It costs **£9.75**; bookings open **one week ahead** and close at **11:00 the day before**, after which they cannot be changed, cancelled or refunded. Junior Members must wear a gown to Formal Hall and Super-Hall.

A Junior Member may buy **up to two guest tickets** per Formal Hall, at **£16.45 per guest including VAT**. The host must be present to admit their guests and stay for the whole dinner; if the member who booked does not attend, the guests are not admitted and no refund is given. Wine may be bought at the College Bar or brought in with £2.00 corkage per standard 75cl bottle; larger bottles, beer, spirits, liqueurs and port are not allowed. Super-Halls and themed dinners are booked on Upay with their own guest limits, prices and earlier closing times. The College's [Upay booking page](https://www.pet.cam.ac.uk/booking-function-tickets-upay) says to show your University card at check-in; the undergraduate [living page](https://www.pet.cam.ac.uk/living-undergraduates) describes Formal Hall as a chance to invite guests from other colleges. The older [Formal Hall page](https://www.pet.cam.ac.uk/formal-hall-and-events) (undated, with Easter 2022 menus, six-guest limit and £7.20 price) is out of date; use the handbooks. Guest gown rules are not stated.

**Practical assessment:** a Peterhouse member must book you on Upay by 11:00 the day before and sit through dinner with you; each member can bring at most two guests.

formal.visitors: Yes: the College says Formal Hall is for entertaining guests, including guests from other colleges; a Queens’ member books you through Upay.
formal.bookingSummary: Queens’ member books through Upay
formal.rulesSummary: Up to 5 guests per member; booking closes 14:00 two days before; guests 18+; external group bookings currently not permitted.
formal.formalNights: Wed and Sun, 19:30
formal.guests: Up to 5 guests per member (6 tickets including the member)
formal.booking: Upay; closes 14:00 two days before; the printed confirmation page is the ticket
formal.dress: Gowns must be worn by all members of College; guest gown rule not stated
formal.note:
**Guests from other colleges are explicitly welcome.** Formal Hall is at **19:30 on Wednesday and Sunday** in Cripps Dining Hall. A Queens’ member books through Upay: **up to six tickets, one for themselves and five for guests**, paid at booking. Bookings close at **14:00 two days before** the event. The printed confirmation page acts as the ticket. Formal Hall is limited to 150 places; for more guests or a group booking, contact the Catering Management Team (catering@queens.cam.ac.uk). External group bookings are currently not permitted. Nothing is said about outside students booking on their own.

Guests under 18 are not permitted. Enter Hall by 19:30; latecomers and their guests are refused entry and tickets are not refunded. Gowns must be worn by all members of College; no guest gown rule is stated. Tutorial policy allows at most half a bottle of wine per person, with no spirits or fortified wine, and drinking games are banned. Refund requests go first to the JCR/MCR Steward. No price is published on the page; check it in Upay. [Formal Hall rules and booking](https://www.queens.cam.ac.uk/life-at-queens/catering/formal-hall/).

**Practical assessment:** find a Queens’ member to book you by 14:00 two days before; the five-guest allowance is generous, but organised outside groups are not currently accepted.

formal.visitors: Yes, as a named guest (with your college) of a Robinson member, or in a group booking arranged with Catering, normally on a Tuesday.
formal.bookingSummary: Robinson host books online; groups via Catering
formal.rulesSummary: Up to 3 guests per member; Tuesday groups up to 36 with no member ratio; Friday groups up to 18 at 3 guests per member.
formal.formalNights: Tue and Fri in Full Term; doors open 19:20
formal.guests: Up to 3 guests per member without further permission; more through a group booking
formal.booking: Meal Booking Website (login); opens about six days ahead, closes 17:00 the day before; guests' full names and colleges required
formal.dress: Smart casual; Robinson members must wear gowns
formal.price: Member £14.96, guest £25.83 incl. VAT (undated College pages, as shown on 7 Nov 2026)
formal.note:
Formal Hall is on **Tuesday and Friday in Full Term**; doors open at **19:20**. A member books themselves first and then **up to three guests** on the members-only [Meal Booking Website](https://meal.robinson.cam.ac.uk), entering each guest's full name and college; incomplete names may be refused entry. Places generally go on sale six days ahead (midnight Wednesday for Tuesday, midnight Saturday for Friday) and close at **17:00 the day before**. The undated prices are **£14.96 member / £25.83 guest including VAT**; Robinson members booked as guests pay the guest rate. A late-cancellation fee applies: the [Formal Halls page](https://www.robinson.cam.ac.uk/college-life/formal-halls) gives £8.87 for cancelling less than 24 hours before booking closes, while the [booking procedure](https://www.robinson.cam.ac.uk/college-life/formal-halls/booking-procedure) says places cancelled within 24 hours of the hall incur a fee.

**Groups:** Tuesday is the night for clubs and societies, with **up to 36 people and no member-to-guest ratio**; Friday groups are **up to 18 with three guests per Robinson member**. Bookings with more than three non-member guests must be on a Tuesday and go through the Catering Office: check availability at least 14 days ahead, then hand in the [group booking form](https://www.robinson.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/assets/college-life/GroupBookingFormForFormalHall.pdf) with names, colleges and diets no later than one week before, when payment is taken. The organiser signs an agreement taking responsibility for guests' behaviour and for Robinson members wearing gowns. Dress is smart casual and Robinson members wear gowns. Wine can be bought at the Bar before Hall. Drinking games and excessive drinking can lead to removal or a ban.

**Practical assessment:** a Robinson member can bring three guests, and Tuesday group bookings of up to 36 make organised visits comparatively easy if arranged two weeks ahead.

formal.visitors: Yes: the student guide names guests from other colleges; a Selwyn student books you as one of their guests and is responsible for you.
formal.bookingSummary: Selwyn host books online
formal.rulesSummary: 2 guests per student online; up to 2 more if the Deans agree; guests over 16; no booking others' guests; big groups need a private dinner.
formal.formalNights: Tue and Thu in term, 19:30; doors close at 19:30
formal.guests: Up to 2 guests online; the Deans may allow up to 2 more who are personally known to the host
formal.booking: Online through the College member portal (login); no public cutoff
formal.dress: Gowns and formal dress (jacket and tie or equivalent); no jeans, shorts, cropped tops or trainers
formal.price: 2026-27: undergraduate schedule £18.25 member / £21.95 guest; postgraduate schedule £17.75 / £21.30
formal.note:
Formal Hall is on **Tuesday and Thursday at 19:30** during term. The student guide describes it as an occasion to invite guests **from other colleges and outside Cambridge**. A student can book **up to two guests online**; if space permits, the Deans will consider requests for **up to two more**, provided the guests are personally known to the host. Members must not book guest tickets for other people's guests, and Formal Hall cannot be used to entertain large groups, including university clubs and societies, which should book a separate dinner through the Conference Office. All guests must be **over 16**. Booking is through Selwyn's members-only portal; no public booking cutoff was found. The 2026-27 charges are **£18.25 member / £21.95 guest** in the [undergraduate schedule](https://www.sel.cam.ac.uk/ughandbook/finance/summary-undergraduate-fees-charges) and **£17.75 / £21.30** in the [postgraduate schedule](https://www.sel.cam.ac.uk/pghandbook/finance/summary-postgraduate-fees-charges), subject to review. [Food and drink](https://www.sel.cam.ac.uk/ughandbook/facilities/food-and-drink).

Entry usually begins by 19:10, the Porter checks names against the booking list, and doors close promptly at 19:30. Gowns are worn with formal dress (jacket and tie or equivalent); jeans, shorts, cropped tops and trainers are not allowed. Checks include a maximum of one bottle of wine per person, and drinking games are prohibited. Hosts are responsible for their guests. [Formal-dinner rules](https://www.sel.cam.ac.uk/ughandbook/discipline/formal-dinners).

**Practical assessment:** a Selwyn student can bring you as one of two guests; more needs the Deans' agreement, and groups need a separate private dinner.

formal.visitors: Yes: College Regulation G11 provides for guests from other colleges; a Sidney student books you in SidNet and the charge goes on their College account.
formal.bookingSummary: Sidney host books in SidNet
formal.rulesSummary: Up to 3 adult guests per student, charged to their account; other-college guests encouraged, not required, to wear gowns; no spirits.
formal.formalNights: Wed, Fri, Sun in term; 19:30 (SSCSU)
formal.guests: Up to 3 guests aged 18+ who are not College members; younger siblings only with Domestic Bursar permission
formal.booking: SidNet (login); up to a fortnight ahead per the undated SSCSU page; cutoff not published
formal.dress: Students wear gowns with formal dress; other-college guests may wear their gown and are encouraged to
formal.price: 2026-27: £14.50 student, £19.95 guest (College finance and funding page)
formal.note:
Formal Hall is held **three times a week** ([College dining](https://www.sid.cam.ac.uk/life-sidney/food-and-facilities/eating-here)); the College's [finance and funding page](https://www.sid.cam.ac.uk/apply/undergraduate-study/covering-costs/finance-and-funding) names **Wednesday, Friday and Sunday** during term, booked through SidNet, and gives **2026-27 prices of £14.50 for students and £19.95 for guests**. The undated [SSCSU Hall guide](https://www.sscsu.org.uk/hall) adds a 19:30 start and booking up to a fortnight ahead. White Book [Regulation G11](https://www.sid.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/G11_College%20Hall20241120.pdf) (file dated 20 November 2024, still linked from the [publications and governance page](https://www.sid.cam.ac.uk/about-sidney/published-information/publications-and-governance)) lets a student bring **up to three adult (18+) guests who are not College members**, charged to the student's College account. A guest from another college may, but need not, wear their gown, and the host should encourage it. No public booking cutoff was found.

Students must normally wear a gown with formal dress or be refused entry. Younger guests need the Domestic Bursar's advance permission: the minimum is 14, or 12-13 with a parent or guardian throughout. Staff may ask for a guest's name and college, and the College can ask any guest to leave. G11 allows students and guests to bring their own wine and drinks but **not spirits**, or to buy wine at the Buttery; staff may limit alcohol, and drinking games and drunkenness are banned. **Source conflict:** the undated SSCSU page says wine must be bought from the Buttery; follow G11 and check on the night. The SSCSU page's £9 / £12.65 prices are older than the College's 2026-27 figures.

**Practical assessment:** a Sidney student can bring you as one of three adult guests, booked in SidNet; finding a host is the main step.

formal.visitors: Only St Catharine’s members and their guests may attend, so a student from another college needs a member to book them as a named guest and enter Hall with them.
formal.bookingSummary: St Catharine’s member books guests on Upay
formal.rulesSummary: Only members and their guests. MCR: up to 3 guests (1 at SCR formals). Upay closes 13:00 on set days; seated by 19:30.
formal.formalNights: Wed (undergraduate), Thu (postgraduate) and Sun in term; Super Hall on a Friday twice a term; seated by 19:30
formal.guests: MCR guide: up to 3 guests per member at a Thursday formal in Hall, 1 at the monthly SCR formal; College page gives no general cap
formal.booking: Upay; MCR says booking opens two weeks ahead. Closes 13:00 on Sun (for Wed), Mon (Thu), Tue (Fri) or Thu (Sun); no cancellation or refund after close
formal.dress: Members wear gowns; guests may. Suit or trousers and jacket, collared shirt, tie and shoes (not trainers or sandals), or equivalent
formal.note:
The College lists undergraduate formals on **Wednesday**, postgraduate formals on **Thursday**, a formal on **Sunday**, and a Super Hall on a Friday twice each term. Bookings are made on Upay and close at **13:00** on Sunday (for Wednesday), Monday (Thursday), Tuesday (Friday) and Thursday (Sunday); after closing there is no cancellation or refund. Members must bring their University Card and enter Hall with all their guests. Under-16s are not admitted, and 16–18s need the Dean's prior permission. [College formal halls page](https://www.caths.cam.ac.uk/students/college-facilities-and-forms/catering-for-our-community/formal-hall)

The College's code says **only members of St Catharine’s and their guests** may attend, guests' names must be entered when booking, names cannot be changed after booking closes, and diners must be seated by **19:30**; latecomers are refused. Formal Hall is not for large groups or societies, which must book private dinners. Each person may bring one bottle of wine or soft drink; no other alcohol. [Formal Hall Code of Behaviour](https://www.caths.cam.ac.uk/students/college-facilities-and-forms/catering-for-our-community/formal-hall-code-behaviour)

The MCR guide adds that bookings open two weeks before. A member may book **up to three guests** for a Thursday formal in Hall, but only **one** at the monthly formal in the smaller SCR (capacity 40). Pre-drinks start at 18:45; the group goes to Hall at 19:20, and there is no entry after 19:30. Pre-drinks and port with the cheese course are provided, and corkage is free. Members wear gowns; guests may. Sunday formals are shared with the JCR. The MCR says its **outgoing swaps** to other colleges have only 10–20 places; this says nothing about places for visitors to St Catharine’s. No price is published; Upay shows it. [MCR formal hall guide](https://mcr.caths.cam.ac.uk/hallinfo)

**Practical assessment:** A visitor needs a St Catharine’s member to book them as a named guest on Upay and to enter Hall with them. Watch the 13:00 closing day for each formal night. Guest numbers come from the MCR guide; the College pages give no general cap.

formal.visitors: The booking system works only for current St Edmund’s members, so a student from another college can attend only as a guest booked by, and dining with, a member.
formal.bookingSummary: Member books guests on members-only Dinner Booking System
formal.rulesSummary: Guest numbers set per event in the DBS. 2025/26 rules: host must dine with guests, no resale, no late cancellation. Fellowship Dinners invite-only.
formal.formalNights: Most Tuesdays and Fridays in term (start time not published)
formal.guests: As indicated in the Dinner Booking System for each dinner (2025/26 Notes for Members); no fixed cap published
formal.booking: Member books on the Dinner Booking System (current members only), entering guests' names; cancel before the list closes or pay in full (2025/26 rules)
formal.dress: Business attire with academic gown for most weekday formals; 2025/26 Notes: formal dress and gowns at Formal Hall
formal.note:
The College holds optional Formal Halls **twice a week, on most Tuesdays and Fridays**. For most weekday dinners the dress code is business attire with an academic gown. [College dining page](https://www.st-edmunds.cam.ac.uk/college-life/dining/) Bookings go through the [Dinner Booking System](https://my.st-edmunds.cam.ac.uk/dinner-booking-system/), and the College says the link **only works for current members of St Edmund’s**. [Part-time study page](https://www.st-edmunds.cam.ac.uk/part-time-study-at-st-edmunds/)

The latest public rules are in the **2025/26** Notes for Members; the College's Notes page now needs a login, so no 2026/27 version could be checked. Under the 2025/26 rules, members enter their own and their guests' names on the system. Guests must be **accompanied at the meal by the member who booked them**, resale of places is not permitted, and children under 16 are not admitted. Members may normally invite guests **as indicated in the DBS**; no fixed number is published. Formal Hall is a three-course meal including wine; members must not bring wine into the Dining Hall. Phones and laptops must be put away, and photography is not permitted. Cancellations go through the DBS until the list closes. After that the full charge applies unless the Fellows' Stewards reallocate the place to the standby list, and private arrangements between individuals are not allowed. Prices are set each Easter Term for the following year but are not published. **Fellowship Dinners** are open to Fellows by invitation only. Admissions and Matriculation Dinners are only for new members, Fellows and the CR Executive. [Notes for Members 2025/26, §7](https://www.st-edmunds.cam.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Notes-for-Members-2025-26-v1.2.pdf)

**Practical assessment:** A visitor needs a current St Edmund’s member to book them through the DBS and dine with them. Check the guest allowance and closing time shown for that dinner. The detailed rules come from the 2025/26 Notes and may have changed.

formal.visitors: No public rule lets outsiders book directly; a student from another college attends as a St John’s student's guest, and the host is responsible for them.
formal.bookingSummary: St John’s student books guests on Upay
formal.rulesSummary: College code: Dean's permission needed for more than 2 guests (SBR guide says 4). Upay closes 09:00 the day before (Fri for Sun).
formal.formalNights: Tue–Fri and Sun in term, 19:30 (SBR guide 2026); College says five days a week
formal.guests: College Guide to Student Behaviour (25 Sep 2026): more than 2 guests needs the Dean for Student Conduct's permission; the SBR guide says up to 4
formal.booking: Upay, before 09:00 the day before (09:00 Friday for Sunday), per SBR guide 2026
formal.dress: Gowns required; SBR guide says no other dress code, though most dress formally
formal.price: SBR Postgraduate Freshers' Guide 2026: guests around £25.20 with wine, £19.39 without
formal.note:
The College says there are **150 Formal Hall tickets five days a week**, students wear black gowns, and students are welcome to bring friends or guests. [College food and drink page](https://www.joh.cam.ac.uk/live-and-study/food-and-drink)

The SBR's **Postgraduate Freshers' Guide 2026**, an informal guide written by the postgraduate committee, gives the details. Dinners run every evening except Monday and Saturday in term. Tickets are bought on Upay **before 09:00 the day before** (09:00 Friday for Sunday). Prices are around **£25.20 with wine / £19.39 without for guests** (£19.20 / £13.18 for members). Dinner starts at **19:30 sharp** and latecomers are not admitted. You need your University Card to be checked in. Apart from gowns there is no dress code, though most people dress fairly formally. The guide says members may take **up to four guests**. BA Table (Tuesday and Friday, postgraduates only) is a separate Upay ticket that often sells out, and Superhalls may sell out quickly. [SBR Postgraduate Freshers' Guide 2026](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1vPmbdIw2yIEAaw-goCRs07Y6I4Q2S2XQ/view)

**Conflict:** the College's **Guide to Student Behaviour, updated 25 September 2026**, §6.6, says students need the Dean for Student Conduct's permission to bring **more than 2 guests** to Formal Hall. Under §6.7, students are responsible for their guests' behaviour. Treat two as the ordinary allowance. [Guide to Student Behaviour](https://johnscam.lon1.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/STATEMENTS%20&%20REPORTS/25-09-26%20Guide%20to%20Student%20Behaviour.pdf)

**Practical assessment:** A visitor needs a St John’s student to book them on Upay by 09:00 the day before. Without the Dean's permission, that student can bring two guests at most. Prices come from the SBR's informal guide; check Upay for the actual rate.

formal.visitors: A student from another college can attend as one Trinity student's named guest, accompanied throughout, or through an exchange dinner run by a Trinity college society with its counterpart society.
formal.bookingSummary: Trinity student books one guest on Upay
formal.rulesSummary: One guest when capacity allows; extra guest by request 10 days ahead. Upay opens 10 days, closes 3 days before (20:00). Host stays with guests.
formal.formalNights: Thu and Sat in Full Term (Sat only in Easter Term), 20:00
formal.guests: One guest when there is capacity; in exceptional cases one extra guest by emailing the Head of Catering ten days before
formal.booking: Upay: opens ten days before (08:00), closes three days before (20:00); sales final after closing
formal.dress: Smart dress and gowns (academical dress) at Formal Hall
formal.note:
The **2026–27 White Book** (revised August 2026) lists Formal Hall at **20:00 on Thursday and Saturday** in Full Term, Saturday only in Easter Term. The postgraduate BA Dinner on Friday is separate. Students buy tickets on Upay. Booking opens **ten days before (08:00)** and closes **three days before (20:00)**, after which sales are final and non-refundable. Upay shows the price; the White Book gives no figure. When there is capacity, a student may bring **one guest** at a time. In exceptional cases, a student may request **one additional guest ticket** by emailing the Head of Catering **ten days before**, with a justification and all guests' full names. Hosts must accompany their guests **at all times** on College premises and enter guests' correct names. Guests must identify themselves and their host when asked. Under-18s need the Head of Catering's prior permission, and under-16s may not dine. Smart dress and gowns are worn. Photography and phones are not permitted, and students found taking part in drinking games are ejected. Some special dinners do not allow guests.

Seating follows the High Table convention: places cannot be reserved, and the White Book says groups should make other arrangements. **University societies** may not dine in Hall without extraordinary College Council permission. Trinity **college societies** may introduce guests from counterpart college societies at formal hall exchange dinners. [White Book 2026–27, §§42, 43, 45, 51, 57](https://www.trin.cam.ac.uk/download/the-white-book/?masterkey=5fe2b486e8747&wpdmdl=1228) The [Postdoctoral Society page](https://postdocsoc.trin.cam.ac.uk/formal-halls/) gives the same ten-day/three-day Upay window for postdoc bookings.

**Practical assessment:** A visitor needs a Trinity student to book them as their single guest on Upay three to ten days ahead and to stay with them throughout. Exchanges between college societies are the only documented group route.

formal.visitors: No public rule lets outsiders book; a student from another college attends as a member's guest or through an MCR exchange dinner.
formal.bookingSummary: Trinity Hall host books, or an MCR exchange dinner
formal.rulesSummary: Formal Thu and Sun in term, Super Halls on some Fridays. Guest cap, booking deadline, start time and price are not published.
formal.formalNights: Thu and Sun in term (JCR: Full Term); Super Halls usually on Fridays once or twice a term; start time not published
formal.booking: Member books on the College's Meal Booking and Accounts System (Raven login); deadline not published
formal.dress: Smart dress; no jeans, trainers, beach footwear, hats or caps; jackets and gowns kept on. College members wear gowns
formal.note:
The College's incoming-undergraduate page lists Formal Halls on **Thursday and Sunday evenings during term**, with Super Halls usually on Fridays once or twice a term. Places are booked through the Meal Booking and Accounts System on the intranet. [College incoming-student page](https://www.trinhall.cam.ac.uk/information-for-new-undergraduate-students/) The MCR links to the [meal-booking portal](https://mcr.trinhall.cam.ac.uk/useful-links/), which requires a Raven login. The College's catering FAQs and swaps-information pages are on the intranet and not public. **No public guest cap, booking deadline, start time or price was found.**

The College dress guide applies to all students and guests: smart dress; no jeans, training shoes, beach footwear, hats or caps; jackets and gowns kept on. Members must make sure their guests comply. [College dress guide](https://www.trinhall.cam.ac.uk/student-hub/guide-to-dress-codes/) The JCR says formals are every Thursday and Sunday in Full Term, members wear gowns, and diners may bring an **unopened bottle of wine**. Superhalls are booked through the same system; gowns are not worn, but there is a no-trainers, no-jeans rule. [JCR food and drink](https://jcr.trinhall.cam.ac.uk/college-life/facilities/food-drink) The MCR constitution makes the External Entertainments Officer responsible for **organising exchange dinners with other colleges**. [MCR constitution](https://mcr.trinhall.cam.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/MCR-Constitution-October-2024-1.pdf)

**Practical assessment:** A visitor needs a Trinity Hall member to book them, or a place at an MCR exchange dinner. Guest numbers and deadlines are only visible inside the College system.

formal.visitors: Yes, as one of up to three guests booked by a Wolfson member, who must attend with them; the student-guest rate applies.
formal.bookingSummary: Wolfson member books up to 3 guests; host attends
formal.rulesSummary: Up to 3 non-Wolfson guests, 18+, with their host. Book or cancel by 12:00 the day before; waitlist. Places cannot be sold or passed on.
formal.formalNights: Tue and Fri in Full Term, Tue at other times; arrive 19:15, dinner 19:30
formal.guests: Up to 3 non-Wolfson guests per member; minimum age 18; must be accompanied by the Wolfson host
formal.booking: Dining Portal, prepaid from University card credit; booking and cancellation close 12:00 the day before; waiting list needs funds
formal.dress: Formal business attire (jacket and tie or equivalent); gowns optional for members and for guests who are University members
formal.price: Student guests £31.56 with wine, £21.36 without (College page, checked 7 Nov 2026; no year stated)
formal.note:
Formal Hall is on **Tuesday and Friday in Full Term and Tuesday at other times**. Diners arrive at **19:15** for drinks and dinner starts at **19:30**. Members book and prepay through the Dining Portal. Booking and cancellation close at **12:00 noon the day before**, and some dates fill earlier. A waiting list books released places automatically, but only if the member has enough funds in their account. Members may bring **up to three non-Wolfson guests**, and all guests must be accompanied by their Wolfson host. The minimum age is 18. Places may not be sold, passed on or given away, even to another member. Diners bring the University Card the booking was made on; anyone without a University Card collects a temporary pass from the Porters' Lodge.

The dress code is formal business attire. Jeans, trainers, beach footwear, shorts, hats and caps are refused entry. Gowns are optional for members and for guests who are University members. Outside drinks, electronic devices and photographs are not allowed. The page lists **student guests at £31.56 with wine / £21.36 without**, with no academic year stated. Groups of ten or more need permission from Conference & Events at least a week ahead. A group may have at most twenty people, there is one group per Formal Hall, and each member may bring up to three guests. [Wolfson Formal Halls page](https://www.wolfson.cam.ac.uk/college-life/food/formal-halls)

**Practical assessment:** A visitor needs a Wolfson member to book them before noon the day before and to attend with them. When a dinner is full, the waiting list is the documented fallback.
